decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'you can just paste the link and hit Save'. R3 client: 'Saving with just the link feels right'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url conforms to reference; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'the title is a separate, optional field you can skip' — no auto-collection presented. R3 client: 'if I leave the title blank, I'd expect the app to automatically pick up the page's real title... Could you adjust the saving flow to fill in that page information automatically?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented save flow omitted automatic metadata collection (REF-BM-02); client supplied the reference-conforming behaviour (auto-fill).

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: list entry displays 'a title, the link itself, and when you saved it' (missing description, tags, favicon). R3 client: 'In the list, I'd like to see the title, a short description, tags, and a small site icon'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented list omitted description/tags/favicon required by REF-BM-07; client supplied the conforming display set.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'a site icon, a title, and a short description filled in automatically' — no preview image. R4 client: 'Yes, this matches what I had in mind... This saving flow works for me.'
decisions.note: Prototype review (revised presentation). REF-BM-02 also requires a preview image, still absent; passed with bare approval and no expression of the difference.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker offered three tagging variants: A 'Suggestions from tags you've used before pop up as you type', B comma-separated, C click-to-reuse. R5 client: 'I prefer Version A... the suggestions make it easy to reuse existing names'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Alternatives differ in fulfilment of autocomplete-of-existing-tags (REF-BM-10); client selected the reference-conforming variant. Offered decision marked diverged=true per select rule.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker offered a 'To read' flag+Mark-read vs opt-in reading list+Done. R6 client: 'Version B matches... pressing Done should remove an item from that list while keeping it saved in my main collection.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Both offered variants are functionally equivalent for read-later/unread-view/mark-read (REF-BM-17/18/19); selection is between equivalent implementations, so not a reference divergence. Client's Done-keeps-saved statement conforms to REF-BM-19.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker: 'Click a tag... The list filters to everything carrying that tag'. R7 client: 'Clicking a tag on a card works well'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Clicking a tag chip to filter is an equivalent UI realising REF-BM-11; conforming.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker: 'I made it match against the title, description, tags, and site name together' (no note, no url). R7 client: 'I'd also expect search to look through the full web address and any notes I've written on a bookmark... With those included, this finding flow would match what I need.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented search scope omitted note and url required by REF-BM-12; client supplied the conforming fields. R8 fulfilled this (linked disposition, not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: R8 maker: click 'Add a note', type text, 'It appears as a highlighted note'; searchable by note. R8 client: 'Yes, this covers the finding flow I need... I'm happy with this flow.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Note-writing/searching is present, but the record does not establish whether the note is markdown-rendered as REF-BM-23 requires; divergence cannot be established, so diverged=null.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker offered only manual title on fetch failure: 'click Add a title yourself'; 'The description and icon would simply stay blank'. R9 client: 'I'd also like the option to add a description manually, though it doesn't need to be required.'
decisions.note: Edge/prototype review. Presented scope offered only manual title; client requested manual description entry, a related reference requirement (editing title/description, REF-BM-03/04) missing from the presented scope.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: 'Remove' asks 'Remove this link for good?' with Remove/Cancel. R10 client: 'A confirmation is enough protection before permanently removing a link.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delete with confirmation conforms to REF-BM-05 (confirm dialog is equivalent UI).

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: re-saving 'tells you you've already saved this and jumps to the existing one'. R10 client: 'telling me and taking me to the existing bookmark is much better than creating another copy.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Duplicate-save converges to the existing item, conforming to REF-BM-06.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker: 'the collection to stay a clean, newest-first scrolling list' with search/filter as the way to cut it down; no selectable sort key offered. R11 client: 'comfortable using search and tag filters as the main way to manage a large collection, with newest-first as the default.'
decisions.note: Prototype/spec review. REF-BM-22 requires user-selectable sort by a key (date, title, etc.); only a fixed newest-first default was presented. Client accepted the default without expressing an expectation of selectable sorting.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker: 'Noted for later, not now: ... export/backup ...' — excluded from build scope. R12 client: 'Yes, that matches what we agreed. Please go ahead and implement it.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Export (REF-BM-31) deferred out of the build scope; client accepted the scope with bare approval and no expression of the difference.
